title: The first request
prompt: Which request makes good use of an agent without giving away the important decisions?

setup.text: Connected to your project. I can read the files, edit them, and run commands like the build. What would you like to do?

options.label: “Build me a polished app. Make whatever decisions you need.”

outcome.text: Done. I scaffolded a new app with a landing page, a pricing page, and a blog, picked a color scheme, and rewrote your homepage copy to match.
Wait. This doesn’t look like my site anymore. Which of these decisions were mine to make?

options.verdict: This delegates the product decisions as well as the typing. There is no shared picture of done, so a confident result can still be the wrong product.

options.label: “Inspect this small site, explain how the homepage is built, then wait.”

outcome.text: It’s a template site with three pages. The homepage text lives in one file, the styles in another, and `npm run build` checks that everything still compiles. Two things stood out: one image is oversized, and a link on the About page is broken. I haven’t changed anything.
Now I can see two small, safe tasks worth trying, and I know how to check them.

options.verdict: This uses the agent’s access to the project while keeping the first move read-only. You get orientation before authorizing change.

options.label: “Tell me how websites work.”

outcome.text: In general: HTML holds the content, CSS controls the appearance, and JavaScript adds behavior. Want me to look at how your project does these things specifically?
Good explanation, and I could have gotten it from any chat. I still haven’t learned anything about my own site.

options.verdict: That is a useful chat question, but it does not use the agent’s ability to inspect your actual project.
